notes: Only scan 103 and its assigned textual packet were used. The original layout view and both native halves were each viewed once. All eight saved crops were then inspected. No original or half was revisited, and no decided place was recropped. No OCR, recognition software, external research or TeX compilation was used.

Original image dimensions are 1690 by 2363 pixels. There is no handwritten authorial folio visible at the head. The only page numeral on this sheet is the pale lower-left 102; its authorship is undetermined.

The opening paragraph states that the structure of S Pi M_G remains to be made explicit in terms of the M_{g_alpha,hatted I_alpha}, and defers that task to the next numbered section. The source gives no numeral for that future section.

The main paragraph asserts that a general normalization morphism yields diagram146 commuting up to isomorphism of functors. The diagonal annotation identifies S-prime with a subset of S and g_alpha with g-prime indexed by alpha-prime. These are manuscript statements, not independently proved conclusions of this collation.
The margin states that the construction comes from an analogous diagram at the level of the modular multiplicities themselves. The words elles-mêmes are visibly present and are retained.

The explanatory paragraph says psi is induced by maps147, given the written inclusion of hatted I-prime_alpha into hatted I_alpha. The last paragraph reduces knowledge of general normalization morphisms to maps148. Their existence, the vertical equivalences and commutativity of146 were not proved in this pass.
A limited index-substitution check was performed and recorded below. It does not prove the geometric or groupoid assertions, and it does not decide the clipped final index.

Diagram146's factors after each product sign are written M with their indices; live Pi-index1 is not added before these factors to regularize them against147 or148. H supplies an extra Pi-index1 before the middle-right factor.

The old upper-left index is crossed, and its live replacement G is written below it; the TeX stacks these old and new readings. The underlying old G-prime remains doubtful. No new historical order beyond visible cancellation and replacement is asserted.

The lower cancelled star-candidate is placed independently beside the product, slightly lowered. It is not fixed inside S-prime's index. Its resemblance in position to the other cancelled small group does not certify either its identity or a shared revision history.

The top connector of146 has a clear right head and a short lower-left return. The complete visible geometry is drawn; the small editorial doubt marker is attached to that return and is not a source question mark. No upper-left wing or ordinary full double-headed arrow is supplied.

In148, two successive right heads and the continuous shaft crossing the target Pi are definite visible geometry. They are reproduced together; neither head is classified as cancelled, and no earlier/later sequence is inferred.

The opener before pas is locally doubtful because its curve merges with the p onset. The dark isolated point after pas is definite and separate from the accent in néc. The complete closing parenthesis after strict is retained.
The abbreviations néc, comm and iso are preserved. Iso has no detached stop. Their expansions appear only in the abbreviations list.

The final text reads est réduit despite the feminine connaissance. The final crossed t is visible and no e follows; the agreement is not repaired. The inserted adjective reads généraux and attaches before est.
H's explanatory note concerning146 is editorial, not additional source prose. Its annotation reading is collated against the visible three-line label, and the label is restored to its arrow.

Certainty-only differences are not counted as settled errors: the opening parenthesis, clipped I index and uncertain lower-group attachment remain doubts. H's omission of visible cancelled groups is recorded even where an editorial note mentions rewriting.
